brief: Tall two-and-a-half-storey brick house built into a hillside: side-gabled roof between stepped parapet end walls with paired chimneys, 6/6 windows with stone sills, and a stone-vaulted cellar exposed on the downhill side. Plain, heavy mining-town Federal style; the street drops steeply past it toward the river.

facade.notes: the Specht House (Galena, 1845): two storeys of brick with stepped parapet gable ends and paired chimneys, shutters; it stands on a corner above a high dry-stone retaining wall with a slanted cellar bulkhead; a small stone outbuilding behind; the sidewalk climbs the hill below the wall

why.note: stepped gables at the chimneys: masonry fire stops, a Galena (and German) habit
Galena's bluffs: every lot terraced on a stone wall
